title: Cōnsonantēs Geminātae et Digrapha Nāsālia
subtitle: Cōnsonantēs geminātae (ππ, λλ, σσ/ττ) et assimilātiō nāsālis ante velārēs (γγ, γκ, γξ, γχ).
objectives: Prōnūntiāre cōnsonantēs geminātās (ππ, λλ, μμ, νν, ρρ, σσ) ut sonōs longiōrēs, distīnctōs ā fōrmā simplicī
Explicāre rēgulam assimilātiōnis nāsālis: γ ante γ, κ, ξ, vel χ sonat ut “ng” Anglicum, nōn ut “g”
Recognōscere ττ Atticum et σσ Iōnicum/commūne Graecum ut duās scrīptūrās eiusdem sonī
Legere corrēctē verba cum cōnsonantibus geminātīs vel digraphīs nāsālibus

content.intro: Cōnsonantēs singulae (π β φ, τ δ θ, κ γ χ, etc.) iam nōtae sunt ex lēctiōne priōre. Haec lēctiō duo phaenomena addit, ambō frequentia in Graecō scrīptō: geminātiōnem (eadem littera bis scrīpta, sonus tenētur longior) et assimilātiōnem nāsālem (γ ante alteram velārem mūtat sonum suum in “ng”).
content.explanation:
Ubi eadem cōnsonāns bis scrībitur (ππ, λλ, μμ, νν, ρρ, σσ), sonus nōn duplicātur in duōs sonōs distīnctōs, sed tenētur longior — sīcut in Ītalicō “pizza” (zz longum) vel Latīnō “ille” (ll longum, sī pronūntiātiō classica Latīna sequitur). Discipulus Anglicē loquēns tendit hanc longitūdinem neglegere; melius est eam ab initiō audīre et imitārī.

Praetereā, ubi γ praecēdit statim aliam litteram velārem (γ, κ, ξ, vel χ), γ nōn sonat “g” sed assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem vēlārem, ut Anglicum “ng” in “sing”: ἄγγελος sonat ferē “ANG-ge-los”. Hoc phaenomenon (“digraphum nāsāle”) iam breviter tāctum est in lēctiōne priōre; hīc vidēs rēgulam plēnē cum omnibus quattuor combīnātiōnibus.

rules.heading: a) Cōnsonantēs Geminātae
rules.body:
ScrīptūraSonusExemplum
ππp longumἹππότης (eques)
λλl longumἙλλάς (Graecia)
μμm longumγράμμα (littera)
σσs longum (surdum semper)θάλασσα (mare)
ρρr longum (secunda ρ saepe cum spīritū aspero: ῥρ)Πύρρος (Pyrrhus)

Sonus geminātus nōn est duo sonī sēparātī sed ūnus sonus tentus longius — comparā “bookkeeper” Anglicē (duo k audīta) an “pizza” Ītalicē (ūnum zz longum): Graecum sequitur secundum modellum.

rules.heading: b) Assimilātiō Nāsālis: γ ante γ κ ξ χ
rules.body:
DigraphumSonusExemplum
γγ“ng” + “g”, ut “finger” Anglicēἄγγελος (nūntius)
γκ“ng” + “k”, ut “ink” Anglicēἄγκυρα (ancora)
γξ“ng” + “ks”σάλπιγξ (tuba)
γχ“ng” + “kh” (χ aspīrātum)ἔγχος (hasta)

Rēgula sequitur logicam articulātōriam: cōnsonāns nāsālis ante occlūsīvam velārem ipsa fit velāris — comparā Anglicum “think” (n ante th fit dentālis) vel “sink” (n ante k iam fit velāris in vōce nātīvā, quamquam scrīptūra id nōn ostendit). Graecum id ostendit scrīptūrā ipsā.

rules.heading: c) Ττ Atticum vs. Σσ Commūne
rules.body: Multa verba scrībuntur cum ττ in textibus Atticīs (Athēniēnsibus) sed cum σσ in aliīs dialectīs Graecīs (Iōnicā, et posteā in Koinē commūnī): θάλαττα (Atticē) = θάλασσα (commūniter), ambō “mare”. Nōn est error, sed variātiō dialectālis authentica — id ipsum quod hic cursus per tōtum dēmōnstrat, dialectōs Graecās esse dīversitātēs reālēs, nōn errōrēs. Hic cursus generātim praefert fōrmam Atticam (ττ) in exemplīs propriīs, sed utraque fōrma est correcta et invenīs utramque in textibus authenticīs.

examples: γράμμα — littera, scrīptum. (μμ geminātum: m longum)
Πύρρος — Pyrrhus. (ρρ geminātum; secunda ρ cum spīritū aspero)

commonMistakes.wrong: Prōnūntiāre cōnsonantem geminātam (ππ, λλ, etc.) exāctē sīcut fōrmam simplicem, neglēctā longitūdine.
commonMistakes.right: Tenēre sonum longius — geminātiō est rēalis, nōn mēra convention scrībendī.
commonMistakes.why: Errōrēs longitūdinis cōnsonantium possunt significātiōnem verbī mūtāre, sīcut longitūdō vōcālium.

commonMistakes.wrong: Prōnūntiāre γ ante γ/κ/ξ/χ sīcut “g” normāle, ignōrandō assimilātiōnem nāsālem.
commonMistakes.right: Efferre γ in hāc positiōne ut “ng” (sonum nāsālem vēlārem), nōn ut occlūsīvam “g” plēnam.
commonMistakes.why: Rēgula assimilātiōnis est systemātica et exceptiōnibus caret in hīs quattuor combīnātiōnibus.

commonMistakes.wrong: Crēdere θάλαττα et θάλασσα esse duo verba dīversa cum significātiōnibus dīversīs.
commonMistakes.right: Recognōscere ambās fōrmās ut variantēs dialectālēs (Atticam/commūnem) ūnīus eiusdemque verbī.
commonMistakes.why: Variātiō ττ/σσ est ūnum ex clārissimīs exemplīs dialectī Atticae vs. reliquae Graeciae.

items.prompt: Quōmodo sonat cōnsonāns gemināta (ut ππ) in Graecō?
options: ut duo sonī omnīnō sēparātī cum pausā
items.explanation: Geminātiō indicat longitūdinem sonī, nōn duōs sonōs sēparātōs neque nūllam differentiam.
Prīma γ ante alteram γ assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem vēlārem “ng”.

items.prompt: Quod verbum est fōrma Attica prō “mare”?
items.explanation: Ττ est fōrma Attica proprissima; σσ est fōrma commūnior in aliīs dialectīs et in Koinē.

items.prompt: Ante quās litterās γ assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem?
options: ante γ, κ, ξ, χ tantum
items.explanation: Assimilātiō nāsālis occurrit tantum ante alterās velārēs: γ, κ, ξ, χ.

items.prompt: Quid indicat σσ/ττ variātiō in verbīs sīcut θάλασσα/θάλαττα?
items.explanation: Est variātiō dialectālis rēalis, nōn error nec discrīmen significātiōnis.

exercises.title: Iunge Digraphum cum Sonō
exercises.instructions: Iunge quodque digraphum nāsāle cum sonō suō.

items.explanation: Assimilātiō nāsālis sequitur locum articulātiōnis cōnsonantis sequentis; ττ/σσ sunt variātiō dialectālis, nōn assimilātiō.

exercises.title: Vērum an Falsum
exercises.instructions: Dēcerne utrum vērum an falsum sit.

items.statement: Cōnsonāns gemināta (ut λλ) sonat exāctē sīcut fōrma simplex (ut λ).
Γ ante κ (ut in ἄγκυρα) assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem “ng”.
items.explanation: Corrēctum: assimilātiō nāsālis occurrit ante omnem velārem (γ, κ, ξ, χ).

items.statement: Θάλαττα et θάλασσα sunt duo verba dīversa cum significātiōnibus dīversīs.
items.explanation: Falsum: sunt variantēs dialectālēs (Attica/commūnis) ūnīus eiusdemque verbī, “mare”.

items.statement: Assimilātiō nāsālis γ occurrit tantum ante vōcālēs.
items.explanation: Falsum: occurrit ante cōnsonantēs velārēs (γ, κ, ξ, χ), nōn ante vōcālēs.

summary: Cōnsonantēs geminātae (ππ, λλ, μμ, νν, ρρ, σσ) sonant longius, nōn ut duo sonī sēparātī.
Γ ante γ, κ, ξ, vel χ assimilātur ad sonum nāsālem “ng” (assimilātiō nāsālis).
Ττ Atticum et σσ commūne (Iōnicum/Koinē) sunt variantēs dialectālēs eiusdem sonī, nōn verba dīversa.
Longitūdō cōnsonantium, sīcut longitūdō vōcālium, potest afficere significātiōnem — numquam neglegenda.
